label: late-episode D2 after a1 -> S1 (common), following a rewarded trial
explanation: Fires only at D2, almost exclusively when the agent chose a1 and reached S1 through the common transition (99% of mass). Its activity also depends on time: it is silent before episode trial ~65, and both rate and magnitude rise toward the end of the episode (60% of mass is in trials 90-99). This matches the model value being low (all mass at value < 7.5). It is much weaker after an unrewarded previous trial (prev_reward 0 rate 0.007 vs 0.028), and adding prev_reward == 1 raises dev F1 from 0.74 to 0.83. It never fires at D1/GO, after a2 or S2, or on rare transitions. Every variable in the predicate is observed at D2: the action, the state, the previous reward, and episode time, which the agent can track implicitly. Its correlation with good == S1 follows from the a1/S1 condition. Residual false positives are late a1->S1c steps with low activation; misses are tiny activations just before trial 70 or after unrewarded trials.

issues: Most of the factual claims hold. On dev the feature is active only at D2 (D1 and GO rates are 0). 99.1% of mass is at action==1 and 100% at state==1, it is silent before trial 60, 60% of mass is in trials 90-99, and all mass is at value < 7.73. Original predicate: dev F1 0.830, test F1 0.818, which matches the report.

The claim 'never fires after a2 or S2, or on rare transitions' is slightly overstated. About 0.9% of mass comes from a2->S1 rare steps, and one top window shows a2 S1R firing at 0.42 of max. This is minor.

Systematic false-positive class the explanation misses: the predicate is true but the feature is completely silent when the previous trial reached S2. With prev_state==2 inside the predicate: 1186 dev steps, precision 0.0. Example: a1 S2R rewarded, then a1 S1c. The prev_reward==1 condition does not cover this case, because the previous S2 visit was rewarded. Adding prev_state != 2 raises dev precision from 0.80 to 0.84 with no loss of recall.

The prev_reward==1 condition is overstated. It mainly matters early (trials 70-79). After an unrewarded S1 trial, late a1->S1c steps (ep_trial >= 80, prev_state==1, prev_reward==0) still fire with precision 0.72. These are not 'tiny activations', as the explanation claims: they make up 6.7% of active steps and 6.4% of mass.

The trial-70 cutoff is soft. Within the predicate, precision is 0.54 for trials 70-79 and 0.95 for trials 80 and later. Activation also seems to build over consecutive a1->S1c trials (for example 0.76 -> 0.81 -> 0.85).

The improved predicate below uses only variables observed at D2: GO action, reached state, previous state and reward, and episode time. Test F1 is 0.879 (precision 0.833, recall 0.931, mass recall 0.979), versus 0.818 for the original.
skeptic.revised_label: late-episode D2 of a1 -> S1 (common) when the previous trial also ended in S1 (rewarded, or any outcome after ~trial 80); silent if the previous trial reached S2

final_label: late-episode D2 of a1 -> S1 (common) when the previous trial also ended in S1 (rewarded, or any outcome after ~trial 80); silent if the previous trial reached S2
